anomalies.obs: On the CAN BUS sheet the two M12 connectors have inconsistent pinouts. J2 (CAN Interface A) carries ESTOP_OUT on pin 7 and 5V_switched_CAN on pin 8. J13 (CAN Interface B) does NOT carry ESTOP_OUT on any pin: pin 7 is 5V_switched_CAN and pin 8 is CAN1_N, which is already present on pin 3 (CAN1_N appears twice on J13).
anomalies.expected: The specification states the e-stop buffer feeds 'an ESTOP_OUT signal shared with the CAN connectors J2/J13', and the two connectors are symmetric 'CAN Interface' M12 ports, so J13 should expose ESTOP_OUT (and 5V_switched_CAN) on the same pins as J2, with no net duplicated across two pins.

evidence.quote: feeding an ESTOP_OUT signal shared with the CAN connectors J2/J13 (Section 1, Safety/e-stop)
CAN BUS sheet, J13 pin labels: 1 ESTOP_SINK2, 2 CAN1_P, 3 CAN1_N, 4 GND, 5 CAN0_P, 6 CAN0_N, 7 5V_switched_CAN, 8 CAN1_N (no ESTOP_OUT); J2 pin 7 = ESTOP_OUT, pin 8 = 5V_switched_CAN

anomalies.impact: ESTOP_OUT is not routed to CAN Interface B, so the e-stop status/output shared with J2 is missing on J13. Because the two connectors are intended to use a common harness, J13 pin 8 (CAN1_N) would land on the wire that carries 5V_switched_CAN on J2, shorting the CAN1_N line to the switched 5 V rail (and pin 7 likewise mismatches), which can damage the CAN1 transceiver/bus and break e-stop signalling on that interface.

parsed.summary: The build appears to contain a wiring error on the CAN Interface B connector: J13's pinout does not match J2's, ESTOP_OUT (which the spec says is shared with both J2 and J13) is absent from J13, and CAN1_N is duplicated on J13 pins 3 and 8, which would bridge CAN1_N to the 5V_switched_CAN harness pin. Other spec-flagged items (16 MHz crystals, SM712 TVS arrays, LTC4412, ISL54222, e-stop buffers, GLOBAL_EN/SW1) check out against the drawing.
